etymologies.heading: Etymology
paragraphs: From Middle French vérisimilitude, from Latin vērīsimilitūdō (“likeness to truth”), more correctly written separately as vērī similitūdō; from vērī, genitive singular of vērus (“true, real”), + similitūdō (“likeness, resemblance”).
senses: The property of seeming true, of resembling reality; resemblance to reality.
A statement which merely appears to be true.
